newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil sets high oil recovery goal at Statfjord.
newsitem.headline: Statoil sets high oil recovery goal at Statfjord.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil) said on Thursday the Statfjord field in the North Sea will yield 4.4 billion barrels of oil if the company hits its target of recovering 70 percent of the crude in place.
Statoil said new technology made it possible to tap parts of the reservoir which were earlier hard to produce.

The company's Status Weekly newsletter said a recovery factor of 70 percent was well above the average for other fields off Norway, and will allow Statfjord to remain on stream for at least another 23 years to 2020.
Statfjord has so far produced around 3.4 billion barrels. Daily output this year is expected to average 412,000 barrels.
Statoil said the challenge was to find an operating concept, which would maintain profitability at low production rates.
